scoring_justification: Checker recomputes RMSE of model predictions against hidden FEM gold values from paper Table 2, scoring the improvement of OMT over MT.

hidden_assets.purpose: FEM reference effective Young's modulus (GPa) for artificial stainless steel porous structures at 10–90% porosity, used as gold for RMSE calculation.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Table 2, mean values from 30 random FEM simulations
hidden_assets.generation_method: Digitised directly from the published Table 2 in the source paper (Ceramics International 2018).
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the paper's own reported FEM simulation results; using them directly preserves fidelity to the original validation data.

outputs.description: Effective Young's modulus (GPa) predicted by classical MT, merged-pore modified MT (MMT), and open-cell modified MT (OMT) models for the artificial stainless steel case at porosities 10%–90%. The first row is a header with column names porosity,E_MT,E_MMT,E_OMT. For OMT, open porosity φ_open is assumed equal to the total porosity φ. The checker compares these predictions to hidden FEM reference data, evaluating relative error and RMSE improvement of OMT over MT.

output_contract.notes: The task uses the stepwise differential MT scheme with merged and open-cell modifications as described in the paper's sections 2.2.1–2.2.4. Material: stainless steel (E=193 GPa, ν=0.27); pore size distribution: normal distribution, radii 10–100 μm, five equal-width classes, μ=55 μm, σ=31.8 μm. The CSV must include a header row with column names porosity,E_MT,E_MMT,E_OMT; porosity values are integer percents 10,20,...,90. For OMT, open porosity φ_open is equal to total porosity φ.

steps.description: Validate CSV structure, required columns, non-negative values, and sanity bounds.
Recompute RMSE of model predictions against hidden FEM gold; score full if OMT RMSE < MT RMSE (improvement over classic MT).
